import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("VRPTW")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    n_customers = 9
    n_vehicles = 5
    Q = 50  # vehicle capacity
    vehicle_fixed_cost = 100.0
    depot = [50, 50]
    customers = [[18, 61], [19, 34], [71, 22], [61, 79], [62, 85], [60, 77], [88, 22], [37, 12], [60, 70]]
    demands = [9, 5, 21, 13, 5, 25, 25, 13, 9]
    time_windows = [[0, 288], [58, 127], [31, 83], [53, 127], [26, 106], [53, 126], [50, 110], [51, 115], [36, 109], [44, 99]]
    service_times = [11, 7, 5, 6, 8, 6, 14, 10, 10]

    # Node 0 = depot, nodes 1..N = customers
    N = n_customers
    nodes = list(range(N + 1))
    cust_nodes = list(range(1, N + 1))

    # Coordinates: index 0 = depot, 1..N = customers
    coords = [depot] + customers

    # COMPUTE distance matrix from coordinates
    dist = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                dist[(i,j)] = math.sqrt(
                    (coords[i][0]-coords[j][0])**2 +
                    (coords[i][1]-coords[j][1])**2)

    # Service time by node (depot = 0)
    svc = [0] + service_times

    # Big-M for time linking
    T_max = time_windows[0][1]
    max_svc = max(service_times)
    max_dist = max(dist.values())
    M = T_max + max_svc + max_dist + 1

    # --- Variables ---
    # Arc variables (binary)
    x = {}
    for i in nodes:
        for j in nodes:
            if i != j:
                x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Arc_{i}_{j}")

    # Load variables (MTZ subtour elimination)
    u = {}
    for i in cust_nodes:
        u[i] = m.addVar(lb=demands[i-1], ub=Q, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Load_{i}")

    # Time variables
    t = {}
    for i in nodes:
        a, b = time_windows[i]
        t[i] = m.addVar(lb=a, ub=b, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Time_{i}")
    # Fix depot departure to time 0
    t[0].ub = 0.0

    # --- Objective ---
    # Minimize travel distance + vehicle fixed costs
    obj = quicksum(dist[(i,j)] * x[(i,j)] for i in nodes for j in nodes if i != j)
    obj += quicksum(vehicle_fixed_cost * x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes)
    m.setObjective(obj, GRB.MINIMIZE)

    # --- Constraints ---
    # 1. Each customer has exactly one outgoing arc
    for i in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in nodes if j != i) == 1,
            name=f"VisitOut_C{i}")

    # 2. Each customer has exactly one incoming arc
    for j in cust_nodes:
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in nodes if i != j) == 1,
            name=f"VisitIn_C{j}")

    # 3. At most K vehicles leave the depot
    m.addConstr(
        quicksum(x[(0,j)] for j in cust_nodes) <= n_vehicles,
        name="VehicleLimit")

    # 4. MTZ subtour elimination
    for i in cust_nodes:
        for j in cust_nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    u[i] - u[j] + Q * x[(i,j)] <= Q - demands[j-1],
                    name=f"MTZ_{i}_{j}")

    # 5. Time linking: if arc (i,j) is used, arrival at j >= departure from i
    for j in cust_nodes:
        for i in nodes:
            if i != j:
                m.addConstr(
                    t[i] - t[j] + M * x[(i,j)] <= M - svc[i] - dist[(i,j)],
                    name=f"TimeLink_{i}_{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Dispatch and Route Planning Team
From: Logistics Operations Manager
Subject: Single-day vehicle routing and delivery schedule with time windows and capacity

Overview
We operate a fleet of identical delivery vehicles from a single central depot to serve a set of customer locations over a single planning horizon. All vehicles are dispatched at time 0. Each vehicle undertakes one outbound trip from the depot, visits an assigned sequence of customers, and returns to the depot before closing. Travel time between any two locations is measured as straight-line distance between their coordinates. With an implicit speed of 1, one unit of distance equals one unit of travel time.

Routing and Scheduling Challenge
We must determine which customers each vehicle will serve, the order in which they will be visited, and the planned start time of service at each stop. Every customer must be visited exactly once. Routes must begin at the depot at time 0 and end back at the depot no later than the depot’s closing time. Vehicles are identical in capacity and operating characteristics, and each deployed vehicle incurs a fixed deployment cost in addition to the distance-based travel cost.

Service-Time and Time-Window Requirements
- Time windows: Each customer has an earliest and latest acceptable start time for delivery. The delivery must start within this window. If a vehicle arrives before the earliest time, it must wait on site until the window opens.
- Service times: Each stop requires an unloading/service duration. The vehicle departs the location immediately after service is completed. If the vehicle had to wait for a window to open, service begins at the window opening and departure follows service completion accordingly.

Capacity and Load Feasibility
- Vehicle capacity: Each vehicle can carry a limited load. The total demand assigned to a vehicle’s route must not exceed its capacity at any point in the route.
- Customer demand: Each customer requires a specific quantity of goods. As deliveries are completed, the on-board load decreases by the amount delivered at that stop. Split deliveries are not allowed; each customer is served in full by a single visit.

Cost Considerations
- Distance-based cost: Total travel distance across all used vehicles contributes to variable operating costs.
- Vehicle deployment cost: Activating a vehicle for the day adds a fixed cost per vehicle, incurred only for vehicles that are actually used.

Planning Goal
Build a set of feasible, single-trip routes that collectively visit every customer exactly once, respect all time windows and service times, satisfy vehicle capacity limits, and ensure all vehicles return to the depot before closing. Among all feasible plans, we aim to minimize the sum of total travel distance and vehicle deployment costs.
